diagnostic_evidence.quote: These terms ensure that the weights remain controlled and do not deviate significantly from the constant function \(1\).

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption A2 bounds each individual network, not the family over which maximization occurs. Set all weights to 1 except the initial-data weight φθ7=c. The objective's leading coefficient in c is λ||u0||²/|Γ|−ρ|Ω|. For sufficiently large admissible initial data this is positive, so the supremum is infinite for every state/control candidate. Large reachable data are allowed, for example by scaling a smooth stationary internally controlled state. A negative quadratic penalty cannot dominate an arbitrarily large positive quadratic residual.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose a parameter-independent bounded admissible weight class, as already done in the experiments, and use infimum/supremum unless attainment is established. Any claimed closeness to 1 must follow from an explicit restriction or a proved coercivity condition.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical min–max procedure can have infinite value, and the claimed penalty-based control of the weights is false. Bounds for fixed weight parameters do not establish convergence of this maximization problem.
issues.title: The weight penalty does not make the inner maximization finite
issues.why_classification: A bounded adversary class is a source-supported, contained modification that preserves the PDE settings and adaptive-weight method, but materially changes the stated unrestricted optimization problem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the formulation reduces to the original PDE.

issues.failure_explanation: In both two-dimensional examples, penalizing every ambient spatial derivative on every boundary face penalizes the normal derivative as well as tangential derivatives. Homogeneous Dirichlet data imply only that derivatives of the boundary trace vanish. For example, the exact heat solution e^(−2π²t)sin(πx1)sin(πx2), with f=0, has nonzero normal derivative and therefore positive displayed boundary loss even when every weight is 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the full spatial boundary gradient by its tangential projection, or otherwise remove the normal-derivative penalties from the Dirichlet residual.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative training constructions do not faithfully encode the stated Dirichlet control problems and can penalize exact solutions.
issues.title: The illustrative boundary losses impose unwanted normal-derivative conditions
issues.why_classification: Tangential projection is a local correction to the illustrative losses; it preserves the intended boundary conditions without changing a rate or requiring a new analytical framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\sigma \in W^{m,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R})$ exhibits nonlinear behavior, and either $\sigma(x)$ or $\sigma(x)/x$ is $m$-th order quasi-decaying.

issues.failure_explanation: The quasi-decay definition requires limits 0 and 1 at negative and positive infinity. Raw tanh has limits −1 and 1, while tanh(x)/x tends to 0 at both ends, so neither alternative holds. Moreover, the piecewise-affine hard activations have zero second derivative on every smooth interval and fail the stipulated nonlinear-behavior condition; they also do not have the second-order Sobolev regularity needed here.

failure_location.quote: These include sigmoid, HardSigmoid, tanh, HardTanh, Softsign, Soft-root-sign (SRS), ELU, SELU, CELU, GELU, SiLU, dSiLU, Softplus, and Mish.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the list at the required derivative order, explicitly distinguish normalized sigmoidal variants from raw activations, and remove the piecewise-affine hard activations from these second-order guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: The prose incorrectly identifies activation families covered by the conditional approximation results. The abstract assumption itself and the ReLU³ experiments are not invalidated by this list.
issues.title: Several listed activations do not satisfy the stated assumption
issues.why_classification: The repair limits the advertised activation coverage rather than merely correcting notation, but leaves the conditional theory and the chosen experimental activation intact.

issues.failure_explanation: An exact solution of the unweighted PDE does not have zero componentwise-weighted residual. Likewise, independently weighting u(0) and u0 leaves a discrepancy even when they agree. The proof nevertheless bounds these residuals solely by approximation errors. The theorem itself is false: take φθ6=0 and all other weights equal to 1. Every candidate then has objective at least λ||u0||²/|Γ|−ρ|Ω|, which is strictly positive for sufficiently large reachable data. This contradicts the asserted bound as δ tends to zero and network sizes increase.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weight complete PDE residuals and complete data discrepancies by common factors, or retreat to weights identically 1. Retaining independently weighted operator and data components requires a new consistency result with additional restrictions or a nonvanishing bias term.
issues.overall_effect: All four weighted approximation theorems lose their vanishing-loss conclusion. The claimed interpretation as merely changing the metric of the original residual is also unsupported.
issues.title: Independent component weights destroy the asserted approximation consistency
issues.why_classification: The counterexample defeats the quantified conclusions themselves. Restoring vanishing-loss consistency requires abandoning a central feature of the proposed weighting construction or replacing its convergence argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same convergence holds in $H^2(Q_T)$ for $\varphi \in H^2(Q_T)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The functions are defined only on QT or qT, but convolution samples outside those domains. No extension is specified. Zero extension does not justify the asserted H² convergence when time-endpoint traces are nonzero. It also does not justify the bilinear proof's uniform mollification estimate: even a nonzero constant f develops a boundary layer under zero extension. The displayed kernel norms over QT similarly need to be taken over the ambient kernel domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: First take bounded Sobolev extensions of u in H² and of the bilinear control in W¹,∞, and an L² extension of the internal control. Mollify these extensions on R^(d+1), using ambient-space kernel norms and domain-dependent extension constants.
issues.overall_effect: The smoothing construction and the convergence estimates feeding all four approximation proofs are not valid as written.
issues.title: Mollification is used without the required domain extensions
issues.why_classification: Standard extension operators provide a local repair on the stated domains, preserving the approximation conclusions and size dependence.

issues.failure_explanation: The approximation theorem is applied to general functions of (t,x) on a (d+1)-dimensional domain, but the exponents use the spatial dimension d. The generic approximation formula displayed in the source uses the input dimension in its denominator. No reduction of the mollified state or control to d variables is established. Thus the invoked rates and the ensuing smoothing/size balance do not follow from that approximation result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the approximation estimate in d+1 variables and redo the size thresholds. Because the statements allow δ-dependent sufficiently large sizes, qualitative δ-approximation can be retained by making the approximation error smaller than δ; the displayed dimension-d quantitative estimates need separate justification.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed Sobolev approximation rates and network-size thresholds in all four existence proofs are unsupported.
issues.title: Spatial dimension is substituted for space–time input dimension
issues.why_classification: A contained dimension-aware rebalancing of smoothing and network sizes is needed, rather than a new global approximation architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \(\mathcal{L}_v\) denote the Lipschitz constant of \(v\).

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed triangle inequality replaces a difference of nonlinear residuals by the residual of a difference. In general v(a)−v(b) is not v(a−b), and Lipschitz continuity does not give this additivity. For example, with unit weights and v≡1, uθ=uε=0, fε=1 and fθ=2, the claimed residual-of-difference decomposition can have zero right-hand side and nonzero left-hand side.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the norm of R̄(uθ,fθ)−R̄(uε,fε), then estimate v(uθ)−v(uε) with the stated Lipschitz constant.
issues.overall_effect: The passage from approximation errors to the final internal-control residual bound contains an invalid inference, independently of the weighted-consistency defect.
issues.title: The nonlinear residual is incorrectly treated as additive
issues.why_classification: This is a local replacement of the faulty nonlinear triangle step and preserves the substantive approximation conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: Existence of a controlled trajectory does not give the asserted cost bound for every control realizing it. Take v=0 and a nonzero smooth w compactly supported in (0,T)×ω. Then u=w with f=wt−Δw, or f=wtt−Δw for the wave equation, has zero initial and terminal data. The neural pair uθ=fθ=0 has maximal penalized loss exactly zero for those same data, yet its distance from (u,f) is positive. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace recovery of an arbitrary prescribed control by a solution-set guarantee, or introduce an identifiability/selection mechanism and prove a new stability theorem for the selected control and admissible neural competitors.

issues.failure_explanation: Even after selecting a minimum-cost control, its cost cannot be uniform over shrinking control regions. Testing the linear controlled equation against a fixed nonzero adjoint solution gives a lower bound proportional to 1/||p||L²(qT), which diverges as ω shrinks. In contrast, the zero neural pair's loss for fixed nonzero initial data and zero target is independent of ω. For waves, boundary strips can shrink while retaining the stated geometric assumptions. Thus QT alone cannot determine the asserted constants.

issues.failure_explanation: At unit weights the lateral loss is (d+1)||uθ||L²(ΣT)²+||∂tuθ||L²(ΣT)², not the H¹(ΣT) norm used in the standard residual. Spatial tangential derivatives are missing. This is substantive: on the unit disk, stationary harmonic functions k^(−1/2)r^k sin(kα), with zero reference data and fθ=0, have these displayed losses tending to zero while their spatial H¹ energy stays bounded away from zero. Thus the missing terms cannot simply be inferred.

issues.failure_explanation: A prescribed terminal L² state and an arbitrary learned forcing do not define a weak backward heat solution. Even when such a solution exists, the asserted terminal-to-past stability is false: a Dirichlet eigenmode e^(−μt)eμ has order-one norm at time 0 and terminal norm e^(−μT). No constant independent of μ can give the displayed estimate. The forward differential inequality is also used in the wrong time direction to produce that estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the two equations gives forcing ∂tuθ−Δuθ+v(uθ)−fθ1ω, not the displayed expression with Vuθ. The missing offset is v(ū)−Vū, equivalently v(uθ)−Vuθ. issues.failure_explanation: The actual integration-by-parts flux involves ∂ν(uθ−ū), not merely ∂νuθ; ū=0 on the boundary does not imply ∂νū=0. The wave proof repeats the same treatment of the boundary flux.

issues.failure_explanation: An upper bound on E′ controls later energies from earlier ones; it does not give the displayed upper bound on E(t) from E(T). A rapidly decreasing scalar energy already disproves that inference. Unlike the heat case, the reversible wave energy identity can support a backward estimate, but the proof must also bound −E′.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\Omega \setminus \omega$ is the closed ball centered at $(1/d,\dots,1/d)$ with radius $3/4$.
The domain \(\omega\subset\Omega\) contains a neighborhood of the boundary \(\partial \Omega\).

issues.failure_explanation: For d=10 the stated center has norm 1/√10, and 1/√10+3/4>1. Thus the excluded closed ball is not contained in the unit ball Ω and cannot equal Ω\ω. Even if the intended complement is its intersection with Ω, it reaches an open boundary cap: the boundary point in the center's direction is only 1−1/√10<3/4 from the center. Hence ω does not contain a neighborhood of the whole boundary.
